results.title: 9 Tasks You Must Do With Your Peonies in September For Massive Blooms next Season
results.description:
There's one date on the calendar that matters more to your peonies than any other, and it's October 1st — not because anything magical happens, but because that's roughly when soil temperature crosses the line where roots can no longer build or heal before winter. More gardeners lose next spring's blooms in the last two weeks of September than any other stretch of the year, and it's almost never neglect. Here are nine specific tasks, each tied to a piece of peony biology, that need to happen before that window closes.

🌸 TASKS COVERED IN THIS VIDEO:
✂️ Task 1: Cut Every Stem To The Ground
🧹 Task 2: Strip The Crown Zone Bare And Bag Everything
🧴 Task 3: Sanitize Your Blades Between Every Plant
📏 Task 4: Measure Your Eye Depth
🌱 Task 5: Lift And Reset Any Peony Planted Too Deep
🔪 Task 6: Divide Mature Crowns And Plant New Bare Roots
💧 Task 7: Fix Drainage Before You Backfill
🌾 Task 8: Feed Low Nitrogen, High Phosphorus And Potassium
❄️ Task 9: Water Deeply, Then Leave The Crown Bare All Winter

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
✅ Why leaving peony foliage standing through fall gives Botrytis paeoniae a place to form hardened sclerotia that survive winter and infect next year's buds the moment they emerge
✅ Why home compost almost never gets hot enough to kill that fungus, and why bagging the debris instead of composting it protects your entire garden, not just the peony bed
✅ The single most common reason a healthy, leafy peony never blooms — and the exact ruler measurement that confirms it
✅ How to lift and reset a too-deep crown without snapping the brittle storage roots, and why it's normal to get fewer blooms the following spring before it comes back stronger
✅ How to divide a mature crown into multiple full plants, how many eyes each division actually needs to bloom within two to three years, and why spacing matters more than most gardeners think
✅ Why September nitrogen works against the plant, and what phosphorus and potassium are actually doing underground right now to shape next spring's bloom count
✅ Why mulching over an established peony crown in fall can cost you flowers — and the one exception where a little mulch is genuinely needed
